description:
## Why
After the rest of fz-nhb, a fixture keeps its .oracle.exs twin only because it tests an fz extension or measures the compiler. Listing them in one place, each with its reason, makes that a fact anyone can check, and shows which twins a later language change would free.

## What changes
.agent/docs/fixtures.md gets a table: stem, the fz-only feature or measurement it covers, and the decision or ticket that keeps it.
- fz extensions (keep): 00633, 00879, 01027, 01111, 01113, 01129, 01419, 01634.
- Whatever the guard, stdlib-name, unquote and fz-nhb.12 (single-use type variable, 01080) decisions keep.
- The pinned four, 00420, 00569, 00571 and 01481, stay in fz form (owner decision, 2026-11-17). Rust tests pin their compile-work counts, which an Elixir rewrite would move (canon 00569 123->118, reach 00420 (68,112)->(67,111), work_start_reason 4->5, public_trace 00571 walks 528->519). Their subject is compiler work, not Elixir output.

## Signal
The table's stems equal `ls fixtures/*.oracle.exs fixtures2/**/*.oracle.exs` exactly.
title: .agent/docs/fixtures.md lists each fixture that keeps an Elixir twin and why
